subject: Post-call: data handling clarifications & retention options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@acmetherapy.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:41:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: data handling clarifications & retention options

Rajiv — thanks again for a productive demo this morning. Quick recap + next steps from my side: 

- Key asks we heard: zero-retention for conversational data (no KV or logs kept), SOC 2 evidence, and EU residency for a future pilot.
- Clarifying question for you: is the zero-retention ask absolute (no ephemeral KV at all), or would a strictly time-limited KV (e.g., <72 hours) be acceptable for producing consistent responses during a user session?

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll pull together a short options letter (privacy-safe alternatives + what we can technically and contractually commit to).
2) Loop in our security lead for concrete controls and SOC2 artifacts.
3) If needed, we can run a short pilot with an isolated tenant and tailored retention settings.

Attaching a brief post-call notes PDF. I’ll follow up with an internal ask to scope the exception path.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme-postcall-notes.pdf
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@acmetherapy.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.legal@acmetherapy.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: data handling clarifications & retention options

Jordan — thanks for the summary and the demo. Helpful. Short answers: 

- Zero-retention is a firm requirement for the pilot clinical workflows we run. Our clinicians cannot have any conversational data retained beyond the immediate session for compliance reasons.
- SOC2 artifacts are required before we proceed to contract.
- Residence: US-only for now (we can revisit EU later).

I understand there are technical trade-offs — if Redwood can provide a design that guarantees no long-term KV or logs and a signed attestation, we can move forward. If not, we’re likely to pause until we find a vendor that can do zero retention.

Can your security lead provide a concrete list of what Redwood can commit to (and what you cannot)? We’ll need that to prepare internal sign-off.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Sharma
Head of Platform, Acme Therapy

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: data handling clarifications & retention options

Jordan / Lauren — quick technical reality check and a suggested compromise we can commit to today: 

- Absolute zero-retention on hosted multi-tenant is not feasible for stateful convo models because we rely on short-lived KV to preserve context across tokens; without any KV the UX/quality will degrade or we must switch to stateless completions (significant feature loss).

- Proposed alternate: a 72-hour KV window combined with TTL-based automated purge, strict access controls (no human access to raw KV), per-tenant encryption keys, and a separate minimal audit log that only records metadata (not full prompts/responses). We can build a contractual attestation that no conversational data will be retained beyond 72 hours and provide SOC2 summary evidence.

- If Acme requires zero-retention in the strictest sense, the only immediate path is a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where we can disable KV at the application layer — this will add ~8-10 weeks and infra costs.

Attachments: retention-alternative-3d.pdf (technical summary + MOP), SOC2-Summary.pdf (already available).

If you want, I can draft the short attestation language for legal.

—Karthik
Principal, Applied ML & Security | Redwood Inference
Attachment: retention-alternative-3d.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@acmetherapy.com>, Emily Chen <emily.legal@acmetherapy.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: data handling clarifications & retention options

Rajiv / Emily — thanks for the candid ask and for elevating the compliance requirement. Per our internal review (Karthik copied):

Proposed pilot commitment (commercial + technical):
- 72-hour KV window with automatic TTL purge. No conversational KV or prompt/response data will be retained beyond 72 hours.
- KV and minimal logs encrypted with tenant-specific KMS keys; access controls and monitoring in place.
- No human access to raw KV contents; we’ll provide process documentation and a signed attestation for procurement.
- We will provide a SOC2 summary and relevant artifacts (see attached).

If Acme needs true zero-retention (no KV ever), we can offer a private deployment option: isolated VPC with application-level KV disabled. Timeline: ~8–10 weeks and additional infra costs; we can scope a pilot statement of work if you want to go that route.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached short proposal (acme-proposed-retention-letter.pdf) and the SOC2 summary.
2) If acceptable, Emily — would you like a one-page attestation drafted for procurement? We can target legal sign-off within 3 business days.
3) Schedule a technical kickoff (Karthik + Eng) to define pilot success criteria.

Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up on Thursday to finalize? I’ll send a calendar invite pending your availability.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme-proposed-retention-letter.pdf, SOC2-Summary.pdf
